facts.text: Barbourmeade takes its name from early settlers Thomas and Richard Barbour, whose family home once sat on a 500‑acre tract along what is now Barbour Lane.
The community’s elementary school honors WAVE founder George Norton Jr., whose leadership helped shape local education.
A planned Louisville‑Interurban Railroad line in the early 1910s would have crossed Barbourmeade, but the project never materialized.
In 1941, Barbourmeade was noted for its fertile soil yet surprisingly inexperienced farmers, as wealthy hobbyists from Louisville settled there.
A modest shopping center erected in 1966 on the Barbour Lane–Brownsboro corner still serves as the community’s commercial hub.
The first liquor store opened in 1978 at the Barbour Lane intersection, its floor crafted from wood reclaimed from Fontaine Ferry Park’s roller‑skating rink.
